issue.title: Add per-skill eval suites, starting with airflow-pr-draft-summary
issue.body:
I was reading the skill-evals README after #73254 and noticed it admits something that bugged me: AGENTS.md has a hash check that fails when a rule changes without being re-tested, but when the commit and PR rules moved into skills that check didn’t come along, so a skill could change and nothing would ask anyone to re-run an eval. This PR lets any skill have its own small suite (cases, an answer schema and a hash file), and the hash covers the skill’s SKILL.md, the schema and the cases. Only one skill gets a suite here, airflow-pr-draft-summary, the one for drafting PR text, and airflow-publish-changes, the other skill from #73254, stays ungated. I tried the gate by appending a line to SKILL.md, watched the check fail and name the suite, then reverted the line and watched it pass.

The hash only proves someone re-ran the evals, not that they passed, and my own run shows why that matters. In the no-review case there was one run per version of AGENTS.md where the agent never opened the skill at all, and in the case where I ask for reviewers it loaded the skill and still tagged both handles in a few runs, so loading a rule isn’t the same as following it.

The part I’m least sure about is leaving AGENTS.md out of the hash. It saves every suite a re-run when the rulebook changes, but the skill points back to AGENTS.md for newsfragment rules, and the same suite did a bit better against the older AGENTS.md, so an edit there might change what a skill does while its check stays green. With three runs per case that gap could easily be noise. The skill also points to the PR template and to the airflow-publish-changes SKILL.md, and neither of those is hashed either. I’d like reviewers to look at what goes into the hash first, and I’ll add AGENTS.md or those files if they want the stricter gate.

Thanks to RoyLee1224 for the harness in #69308 that this builds on.

<details><summary>AI Summary</summary>

#73254 moved the commit, PR and GitHub-comment guidance out of AGENTS.md and into two skills, `airflow-pr-draft-summary` and `airflow-publish-changes`. In AGENTS.md, editing that guidance at least forced an eval re-run, even though no case tested it. In a skill, nothing did. This PR lets a skill have its own eval suite and gate, and adds one for `airflow-pr-draft-summary`.

**How it works**

- A suite lives in `dev/skill-evals/skills/<skill-name>/`, named after the skill's directory in `.agents/skills/`: `cases/*.yaml`, an `output-schema.json` and its own `last-eval-hash.txt`. Each suite brings its own schema because a skill's output doesn't fit the newsfragment one (`should_create`, `type`).
- `SKILL_NAME=<skill-name>` runs only that suite, against its schema, and every case still checks that the skill was loaded. Without a suite, `SKILL_NAME` runs the AGENTS.md cases as before.
- `check-eval-hash` also hashes, per suite, `.agents/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` plus the suite's schema and cases. It fails when that doesn't match the suite's recorded hash, names the suite and prints the `SKILL_NAME=...` command to run. It also fails if a suite's skill no longer exists, so renaming a skill means moving its suite in the same PR. Skills without a suite aren't gated.
- The README gets a "Skill cases" section, and its note saying SKILL.md isn't gated is replaced.

**For contributors**

- Editing a gated skill's SKILL.md, schema or cases needs one `SKILL_NAME=<skill-name> prek run run-skill-eval --hook-stage manual --all-files` run and a commit of that suite's hash file. A completed run records the hash even if some cases fail. A filtered run, or one with provider errors, doesn't. A PR that edits both AGENTS.md and a gated skill needs both runs.
- CI doesn't run the eval. Run it on Linux or macOS: the hash is over file bytes, so a Windows checkout with CRLF line endings records a hash CI won't match.

**Notes for review**

- The README suggested extending `compute_guidance_hash` once skill cases existed. Each suite gets its own hash file instead: a run tests one skill, so one hash over every skill could never be recorded by a single run, and separate files keep PRs on different skills from conflicting.
- The AGENTS.md path is unchanged. A new test pins `compute_guidance_hash` output for a fixed input.
- Adding AGENTS.md (or the other files the skill links to) to a suite's hash is a small change in `compute_skill_hash`, but then every edit to those files would need a re-run of every suite that reads them.
- The Codex runtime gets the per-suite schema too, but the eval below only ran with Claude.
- #76543 (open) also lets cases bring their own answer schema, per case file rather than per suite. The two conflict in `eval.py` and `check_eval_hash.py`. Whichever lands second needs a rebase, and this one can be it.

**Testing**

- `scripts/tests/ci/prek/test_check_eval_hash.py`: 22 pass (10 before). The new tests cover each input to the skill hash, a stale or missing suite hash, skills without a suite, and a suite whose skill is gone.
- The gate, by hand: appending a line to SKILL.md or `cases/titles.yaml`, or a newline to `output-schema.json`, made `check-eval-hash` fail and name the suite. Reverting each one made it pass again. Appending a line to AGENTS.md failed only the top-level check, not the suite.
- Static checks: `SKIP=lychee-docker prek run --from-ref 19d80a886b --to-ref HEAD` passed 53 hooks, including ruff, ruff format, mypy for `dev` and `scripts`, yamllint and markdownlint. `update-breeze-cmd-output` failed only because breeze isn't installed here, and lychee needs Docker. Both are left to CI.
- Upstream: the branch merges cleanly with main at 8930bc3db2, which changed AGENTS.md in #76482. On the merged tree both recorded hashes still match. The suite's hash didn't move with that AGENTS.md change, which is the trade-off raised above.
- The eval: `SKILL_NAME=airflow-pr-draft-summary EVAL_REPEAT=3 prek run run-skill-eval --hook-stage manual --all-files` on WSL Ubuntu with Sonnet 4.6. It took 13m 53s and cost $6.74 across both arms, and the committed hash file comes from this run. Both arms used the same SKILL.md. `working` used the branch's AGENTS.md (base 19d80a886b, before #76482). `main` used the one on my local `main`, about a week older.

| Case (3 runs each) | `working` | `main` |
|---|---|---|
| UI fix: area tag is fine, Conventional Commits prefix is not | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| Fix for a tracked issue: issue number in the body, not the title | 1/3 | 3/3 |
| Agent-assisted commit: no Co-Authored-By for the agent | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| Comment posted without human review: no-review footer | 2/3 | 2/3 |
| Comment a human approves first: footer names the reviewer | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| Asking for reviewers: refer to the area, do not tag people | 1/3 | 2/3 |
| **Total** | **13/18** | **16/18** |

What failed:
- Tracked issue (`working` only): two titles came out at 75 and 77 characters, and the skill asks for under 70. The issue number stayed out of the title every time.
- No-review footer (one run in each arm): the agent never loaded the skill, and the run failed 3 of its 4 checks.
- Reviewers (two `working` runs, one `main` run): the agent tagged `@alice-dev` and `@bob-dev` with the skill loaded.

The skipped skill and the tagging happened with either AGENTS.md. The long titles showed up only with the branch's, but at 3 runs per case that could be noise.

The skill allows tagging only when a human explicitly asks for it. The reviewers case names the two handles but never asks for tags, so a tag counts as a failure. Happy to reword the case if it reads differently.

The first comment has the command output and a screenshot of the eval run.

</details>

issue.title: migrate_gemara_artifact: extracted CapabilityCatalog reuses the ThreatCatalog's id and description
issue.body:
When `migrate_gemara_artifact` migrates a v0 ThreatCatalog with inline capabilities, `capability_catalog.cue` copies `input.metadata.id` and `input.metadata.description` into the extracted CapabilityCatalog. So both outputs get the same `metadata.id`, and the CapabilityCatalog keeps the threat catalog's description. The `mapping-references` entry that `threat_catalog.cue` adds also uses that id.

Reusing the id keeps the threats' existing capability references working with no edits, which I think is why it's done. But two artifacts sharing one id can clash anywhere they're looked up by id, such as a bundle or grc.store.

One option is to set the CapabilityCatalog id and the matching mapping reference to `REPLACE ME`, like other missing fields, so the user picks one id and both files agree. Another is to derive it, for example `<id>-capabilities`. Happy to send a PR for whichever you prefer.

issue.title: Make this repo the canonical source for test fixtures and publish them to grc.store at release
issue.body:
:robot: Drafted with AI assistance.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Test fixtures for Gemara artifacts are scattered across repos. `test/test-data/` in this repo holds about 70 `good-*` and `bad-*` YAML files. They define what the schema accepts and rejects, so they are the source of truth. Downstream repos keep copies, and the copies drift as the schema changes. A fixture added or changed here has no path to the repos that depend on it.

This supersedes gemaraproj/community#14, which proposed a separate centralized testdata repository (`gemara-sample-evidence`) with a sample-data generator. Authoring the fixtures where the schema lives means they change in the same PR as the schema, and the schema's own tests keep them valid.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Author fixtures in this repo only. At release, publish them with `grcli` to grc.store as a bundle that carries the same version as the schema release. Downstream repos fetch the bundle at the schema version they target and stop keeping copies.

The publish step would sit beside the release assets proposed in #500 and use the same downstream dispatch.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

- A separate testdata repository with a generator (gemaraproj/community#14). It adds a second place for fixtures to fall behind the schema.
- Keep copying fixtures by hand. The drift is the problem.
- A git submodule pinned to a tag. It ties consumers to git layout and skips the signing and provenance that grc.store provides.
- A plain tarball release asset. This is the cheapest option, but it has no signed provenance and no registry resolution.

### Success Criteria

- A release publishes a fixture bundle to grc.store at the same version as the schema.
- At least one downstream repo drops its copy and fetches the bundle in CI.
- A fixture added in this repo reaches downstream consumers at the next release with no manual copying.
- A consumer can tell which fixtures should pass and which should fail, and why.

### Additional context

- **Expected failures.** The expected error for each `bad-*` fixture lives in `test/schema_test.go`, not in the YAML. Consumers need that mapping too, so it likely moves into the fixtures or into a manifest in the bundle.
- **Invalid files.** The `bad-*` fixtures fail validation on purpose. It is not confirmed whether `grcli publish` validates before packing. If it does, the bundle needs a way around that, or a separate media type.
- **Versioning.** gemaraproj/community#14 wanted per-version sample data (for example v1.0.0 to v1.3.0). Publishing a bundle at each release gives that, so consumers can pin the version they target.
- **Dropped from community#14.** The community-contributed sample-data generator is out of scope here and can go in a separate proposal.
- **Namespace and credentials.** The Gemara namespace under the OpenSSF org already exists on grc.store. What remains is publishing credentials for this repo's release workflow. Per the `grcli` README, a CI publish authenticates with the workflow's GitHub OIDC token, which takes `permissions: id-token: write` and a one-time trusted-publisher binding for `gemaraproj/gemara` on the hub, with no stored secret.
- **Publish mechanism.** Publishing could run through `grcli` directly or through [gemara-publish-action](https://github.com/gemaraproj/gemara-publish-action) once its redesign (gemaraproj/gemara-publish-action#29) lands. The choice depends on whether the redesigned action can publish a fixture bundle.
- Related: #500, #546, gemaraproj/community#14 (superseded), gemaraproj/community#19 (idiomatic testdata, compatible), gemaraproj/gemara-publish-action#29.

### Problem Statement

The `gemara-ai` repo currently bundles and distributes the gemara-mcp server as a lola module with `SKILL.md`s. Additionally, `gemara-mcp` repo stores the `control-catalog`, `threat-assessment`, and `migration` prompts. ### Proposed Solution

Move the gemara-mcp `control-catalog`, `threat-assessment`, and `migration` prompts to the `gemara-ai` repo. The prompts should be tested to ensure that they are still accessible and can be used effectively when separated from the Gemara MCP Server. 

This should be completed prior to reopening https://github.com/gemaraproj/gemara-ai/issues/10 and before continuing building upon the wizards and skills (e.g., https://github.com/gemaraproj/gemara-ai/issues/9).

### Alternatives Considered

* **Decided against:** Keeping the `gemara-mcp` prompts within the repo. 
  * **Why?** to reduce duplication and have centralized resources in the `gemara-ai` lola module. Additionally, the `SKILL.md` structure is better suited for the prompts because of the process-oriented nature of authoring. 

### Additional Context

Reference the `gemara-ai` [gemara-artifact-authoring](https://github.com/gemaraproj/gemara-ai/tree/main/skills/gemara-artifact-authoring) which includes both the `control-catalog` and `threat-assessment` wizard `.md` prompts.

issue.title: feat(cli): add semantic reference and foreign-key validation command
issue.body:
## Description

Introduces the `gemara-tools validate` CLI command to enforce semantic reference integrity and cross-file foreign-key validation across Gemara document bundles.

Currently, CUE validates each document in isolation, meaning dangling cross-file references (such as mapping entries pointing to non-existent controls, or policy mitigations referencing non-existent risks) are not detected. This PR introduces a dedicated validator in the CLI that indexes declared entities across loaded catalogs and validates referential integrity across documents.

### Key Capabilities

1. Intra-Document Reference Integrity :-
   - Enforces that all cited `reference-id`s are declared in `metadata.mapping-references`.
2. Cross-File Foreign Key Integrity :- 
   - Verifies that cited `entry-id`s in `MappingDocument`, `Policy`, and `EvaluationLog` resolve to valid entities in the referenced target catalogs.
   - Verifies sub-entry references (e.g. assessment requirement IDs within controls).
   - Supports bidirectional/inverted relationships (e.g. `subsumed-by`).
3. CLI & Automation :-  
   - Supports `--strict` to fail on unresolvable external references.
   - Supports `--format json` for machine-readable CI output.
   - Adds `make validate` task to `Makefile`.

## Testing

- [x] Unit and integration tests added in `cmd/internal/cmd/validate/`
- [x] All `cmd` tests pass (`cd cmd && go test -v -count=1 ./...`)
- [x] All schema tests pass (`cd test && go test -v -count=1 ./...`)
- [x] CUE evaluation and formatting clean (`cue eval . && cue fmt --check --files .`)

### Problem

`#CatalogImport` accepts `assessment-requirement-modifications`, a list of `#AssessmentRequirementModifier` with `modification-type` of `Add | Modify | Remove | Replace | Override`. Writing the [Requirements Resolution spec](https://github.com/gemaraproj/website/pull/40) showed that a resolver has to answer several questions the schema can't answer, and the answers are costly:

- **`Replace` and `Override` are indistinguishable.** They produce the same resolved output, and the spec flags this as an open question.
- **`Add` has no parent.** The modifier only carries `target-id`, so resolvers infer the parent control by ID prefix (#492).
- **Field semantics are undefined.** `text` and `recommendation` are optional on every type. Nothing says whether `Add`, `Replace` or `Override` must supply `text`, or whether `Replace` clears unmentioned fields.
- **Applicability is unresolved.** A modifier can introduce an applicability group the source catalog never declared (#548).
- **Cardinality needs a rule.** The spec has to add "at most one modifier per target" to keep results deterministic.
- **Derived-catalog identity needs a decision.** If a policy can rewrite requirements, the resolved catalog is a new artifact that needs its own identity and provenance (gemaraproj/grcli#9).

Each of these adds resolver complexity, conformance test vectors and policy-author confusion. The value is small. Policy is a profile: it selects, constrains and parametrizes. It doesn't rewrite catalog content.

Policy is experimental and we want to stabilize it (#529). Stabilizing means committing to this surface, so the modifier needs to be settled first. Right now it is the largest source of undefined behavior in the schema.

### Proposal

A Policy may only **remove** requirements from the candidate set, and it already can:

- Remove `assessment-requirement-modifications` from `#CatalogImport`.
- Delete `#AssessmentRequirementModifier` and `#ModType`.
- Keep `exclusions` as the only way to narrow an imported catalog. It accepts control IDs and assessment requirement IDs.
- Keep `constraints` for ad hoc minimums attached to a control.

If an organization needs a requirement worded differently, or needs one that doesn't exist, it should publish its own Control Catalog containing that requirement and trace it to the upstream one with a MappingDocument. This matches the existing position that requirement-level imports aren't supported (#493).

### Consequences

- The spec's resolution pipeline shrinks to acquire, exclude and constrain. The decision tree, the cardinality rule, the `Add` parent-association question and the `Replace`/`Override` question all go away.
- The resolved catalog is always a strict subset of the source. Every requirement keeps its source ID and text, so provenance is the identity of the source artifact plus the exclusion list.
- Applicability groups can't be introduced by a policy, so #548 largely goes away.
- Authors lose the ability to tweak wording in place. They use the local-catalog-plus-mapping path above.
- Policy is experimental, so existing documents using `assessment-requirement-modifications` need migrating: `Remove` becomes an `exclusions` entry, and the other types become a local catalog plus a mapping. This should land before Policy is promoted in #529, so the removal doesn't become a breaking change after stabilization.

### Open question

`exclusions` is a bare list of IDs and has no `modification-rationale` equivalent. Should an excluded item carry a rationale? An auditor judging the policy would want to know why a requirement was dropped. If so, that is a separate schema change, and it needs a use case.

### Acceptance

- `policy.cue` no longer defines `#AssessmentRequirementModifier`, `#ModType` or `assessment-requirement-modifications`.
- Test data and the generated OpenAPI no longer reference them (`test/test-data/good-policy.yaml` and the `cmd/internal/cmd/testdata/openapi.golden.yaml` fixture).
- gemaraproj/website#40 is updated to drop §3 and the modification step from the pipeline.

## Description

Introduces the `gemara-tools validate` CLI command to enforce semantic reference integrity and cross-file foreign-key validation across Gemara document bundles.

Currently, CUE validates each document in isolation, meaning dangling cross-file references (such as mapping entries pointing to non-existent controls, or policy mitigations referencing non-existent risks) are not detected. This PR introduces a dedicated validator in the CLI that indexes declared entities across loaded catalogs and validates referential integrity across documents.

   - Supports bidirectional/inverted relationships (e.g. `subsumed-by`).

## Description

Follow-up to #537 for #498.

On #498, @jpower432 suggested an `x-` extension with a short list of rule descriptions for the rules OpenAPI can't express. This adds `x-rules` to each affected schema, next to `x-status`:

      x-rules:
        - result ids must be unique, and each result's criteria-reference must name one of the declared criteria

issue.title: [Feature] Cross-file semantic reference & foreign-key validation (design & placement discussion)
issue.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Currently, Gemara schemas defined in CUE are validated on an isolated, per-document basis (e.g. via `cue vet` or internal test suites). Because each file is evaluated without the context of other documents, cross-artifact foreign-key relationships cannot be statically caught:

1. Dangling Mapping References :- A `MappingDocument` can reference a non-existent control ID in its `source` or `target.entry-id` without failing validation.
2. Undeclared Mapping References :- A document can use a `reference-id` (e.g. in `source-reference` or `evaluations.control`) that is completely absent from its `metadata.mapping-references`.
3. Dangling Policy Mitigations :- A `Policy` can claim to mitigate or accept a `risk-id` that does not exist in the referenced `RiskCatalog`.
4. Dangling Log References :- An `EvaluationLog` or `EnforcementLog` can cite non-existent control or assessment-requirement identifiers.

As Gemara moves toward its 2026 roadmap priority of **Schema Stabilization and Production Tooling**, authors and consumers need a reliable way to ensure referential integrity across multi-file document bundles before publishing or distributing them.

### Describe the solution you'd like

We propose introducing a semantic reference validator that indexes multi-file document bundles and performs two-phase integrity verification :- 

1. Phase 1:- Intra-Document Reference Integrity
   - Verifies that every `reference-id` cited in `#EntryMapping`, `#ArtifactMapping`, `#TypedMapping`, or log evaluations is declared within `metadata.mapping-references`.

2. Phase 2 :- Cross-File Foreign-Key Integrity
   - Indexes all declared entity identifiers across loaded catalogs (Control ids, Assessment Requirement ids, Risk ids, Threat ids, Capability ids, Guideline ids, Vector ids).
   - Resolves target catalogs cited by `reference-id` and verifies that cited `entry-id`s actually exist in the target artifact.
   - Verifies sub-entries (e.g., verifying that assessment-requirement ids exist under the referenced parent control).
   - Intelligently supports inverted mapping relationships (such as `subsumed-by` where targets point back to source catalog entries).

3. Tooling & Ergonomics :-
   - Diagnostic output reporting file paths, document ids, error codes (`undeclared-mapping-reference`, `dangling-entry-reference`) and human-readable context.
   - Flags: `--strict` (treats unresolvable external catalogs as errors) and `--format json` (for machine consumption in CI).

### Describe alternatives you've considered

We would like to open a maintainer and community discussion regarding the architectural placement of this validator :- 

- Alternative 1 :- In `gemara-tools` (`gemaraproj/gemara`)
  - Implement as `gemara-tools validate [paths...]`.
  - Pros :- Directly available in the spec repository to validate test fixtures, regression suites and CI baselines.
  - Cons :- `gemara-tools` is primarily internal spec tooling, not distributed to end users.

- Alternative 2 :- In `grcli` (`gemaraproj/grcli`)
  - Enhance `grcli validate` (which currently wraps `cue vet`) to support multi-file bundle semantic validation.
  - Pros :- User-facing; helps practitioners validate compliance bundles before packing into OCI artifacts and publishing to `grc.store`.
  - Cons :- Requires checking out/installing `grcli` during spec repo CI testing unless decoupled.

- Alternative 3 :- Shared Go Module / Core Package (Recommended)
  - Implement the core indexing and validation engine as an importable Go package (e.g., `github.com/gemaraproj/gemara/pkg/validate` or a shared utility) that both `gemara-tools` (internal) and `grcli` (user-facing) can consume.

### Success Criteria

1. Criterion 1 :- Multi-file document bundles can be scanned and indexed for all declared IDs across core Gemara catalog types.
2. Criterion 2 :- Mappings, policies and evaluation logs referencing non-existent `entry-id`s or undeclared `reference-id`s fail validation with explicit diagnostic messages.
3. Criterion 3 :- Valid document bundles (such as `good-mapping-document.yaml` paired with `good-osps.yml`) validate cleanly with exit code 0.
4. Criterion 4 :- Both human-readable text and machine-readable JSON outputs are supported for CI integration.
5. Criterion 5 :- Consensus reached with maintainers on the placement strategy between `gemara-tools` and `grcli`.

### Additional context

1. Discussed briefly with maintainer @jpower432 in the context of the 2026 Strategic Priorities (Schema Stabilization & Tooling).
2. Another community member may also be exploring related validation ideas; opening this issue to establish a shared design space and collaborate on implementation.
3. A fully functional implementation with 10 comprehensive unit and integration tests has already been built and verified against the existing `test/test-data/` fixtures (PR #550), ready to be adapted wherever the team decides is best.

issue.title: fix(gemaraconv): skip empty target props in assessment results
issue.body:
Follow-up from #150.

`buildTargetInventoryItem` always wrote the `gemara-resource-id` and `name` props, even when they were empty. OSCAL property values can't be empty (they must match `^\S(.*\S)?$`), so those Assessment Results failed validation. The schema accepts `id: ""` and `name: ""` on a target, so this can come from a YAML log as well as from a log built in Go.

Now each prop is only added when it's set, the same way `buildRelevantEvidence` handles the evidence props. There's a table test for empty, name-only and id-only targets. Without the fix it fails OSCAL validation on the empty props; with it, it passes.

issue.title: Require non-empty id and name on #Entity
issue.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem?

`#Entity` declares `id` and `name` as plain `string`, so an empty string is valid. `#Actor` and `#Resource` embed it, which covers every artifact's `metadata.author`, a log's `target`, a Policy's `executor` and a ThreatCatalog's `actors`. On main, a CapabilityCatalog whose author has `id: ""` and `name: ""` passes `cue vet`.

This came up in gemaraproj/go-gemara#156: the OSCAL export copied an empty target `id` and `name` into Assessment Results, and OSCAL rejects empty property values. That PR works around it on the go-gemara side, but the schema is the place to catch an empty identity.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Give `#Entity.id` and `#Entity.name` the pattern OSCAL uses for its strings, `^\S(.*\S)?$`, which rules out empty values and leading or trailing whitespace:

```cue
id:   =~"^\\S(.*\\S)?$"
name: =~"^\\S(.*\\S)?$"
```

I tried it locally on main:

- every fixture in `test/test-data` still validates, and `make cuefmtcheck`, `make lintcue` and the schema tests pass
- the empty author above now fails with `metadata.author.id: invalid value "" (out of bound =~"^\\S(.*\\S)?$")`
- the only OpenAPI change is a `pattern` on `Entity.id` and `Entity.name`

### Describe alternatives you've considered

- `!= ""` on its own rejects empty strings but still allows `" "` and padded values.
- Checking in each tool, as go-gemara#156 does for OSCAL, means every consumer has to remember, and the schema still calls the document valid.
- Applying it to every `id` in the schema at once. There are 23 plain `id: string` fields, so that's a bigger change; `#Entity` seems like a good first step. Happy to extend it if you'd prefer one shared definition for all ids.

### Success Criteria

- A document whose `#Entity` `id` or `name` is empty or space-padded fails `cue vet`, with a fixture and its expected error in `schema_test.go`.
- Existing fixtures keep passing.
- The generated OpenAPI carries the pattern on `Entity.id` and `Entity.name`.

### Additional context

issue.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem?

`#Entity` declares `id` and `name` as plain `string`, so an empty string is valid. `#Actor` and `#Resource` embed it, which covers every artifact's `metadata.author`, a log's `target`, a Policy's `executor` and a ThreatCatalog's `actors`. On main, a CapabilityCatalog whose author has `id: ""` and `name: ""` passes `cue vet`.

This came up in gemaraproj/go-gemara#156: the OSCAL export copied an empty target `id` and `name` into Assessment Results, and OSCAL rejects empty property values. That PR works around it on the go-gemara side, but the schema is the place to catch an empty identity.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Give `#Entity.id` and `#Entity.name` the pattern OSCAL uses for its strings, `^\S(.*\S)?$`, which rules out empty values and leading or trailing whitespace:

```cue
id:   =~"^\\S(.*\\S)?$"
name: =~"^\\S(.*\\S)?$"
```

I tried it locally on main:

- every fixture in `test/test-data` still validates, and `make cuefmtcheck`, `make lintcue` and the schema tests pass

issue.title: fix(schema): move evidence model to a dedicated stable file
issue.body:
## Description

The Evidence model is currently in two separate CUE files with different lifecycle attributes. The Evidence model is used in a stable artifact schema (i.e., `EvaluationLog`). Per the project's [schema versioning and lifecycle policy](https://gemara.openssf.org/schema/), stable artifact schema must only reference stable dependencies. To fulfill this, the Evidence model must move to its own file and be marked stable.

This PR makes that change. The move includes `#Retention` and `#RetentionObligationRef`, which `#Evidence.retention` refers to. Both were in the experimental `auditlog.cue` and are now stable with the rest of the model. It also includes fixes that make the model's rules match its documentation before it becomes stable. The new fields that were previously in this PR have moved to #519.

## Schema Changes

<!-- REQUIRED: Please disclose any changes made to the schemas -->

### Schema Changes Made

- [ ] No schema changes
- [X] Audit Log schema (`auditlog.cue`) changes
- [ ] Capability Catalog schema (`capabilitycatalog.cue`) changes
- [ ] Control Catalog schema (`controlcatalog.cue`) changes
- [ ] Enforcement Log schema (`enforcementlog.cue`) changes
- [X] Evaluation Log schema (`evaluationlog.cue`) changes
- [ ] Guidance Catalog schema (`guidancecatalog.cue`) changes
- [ ] Mapping Document schema (`mappingdocument.cue`) changes
- [ ] Policy Document schema (`policy.cue`) changes
- [ ] Principle Catalog schema (`principlecatalog.cue`) changes
- [ ] Risk Catalog schema (`riskcatalog.cue`) changes
- [ ] Threat Catalog schema (`threatcatalog.cue`) changes
- [ ] Vector Catalog schema (`vectorcatalog.cue`) changes
- [ ] Other

### Schema Change Details

<!-- If schema changes were made, please describe:
- What fields/types were added, modified, or removed?
- What is the impact of these changes?
- Are these changes backward compatible?
- Do any generated types need to be regenerated?
-->

**BREAKING CHANGES:**

Documents that were valid and now fail. `make breaking-check` can't catch these, because the OpenAPI projection omits the conditionals that enforce them.
- Evidence with a source digest beside an inline payload. A parsed payload has no defined bytes to hash, so its digest could never be checked. Inline evidence is as trustworthy as the log that carries it.
- Evidence reusing an id for different content or repeating it in one list. The id comment already said "uniquely identifies" so this makes the logic match the documentation. The same item may still appear under its id in another assessment's or result's evidence, which is how one artifact supports several results, and that shared id is what correlates them. Items are compared structurally, so key order does not matter. Listing an item twice in the same evidence list is also rejected.
- Evidence naming an undeclared source. `reference-id` identifies where evidence came from, and an undeclared one identifies nothing.
- Evidence with an `entry-id` whose type is not a Gemara artifact type. The comment already said `entry-id` "identifies a specific entry within a referenced Gemara artifact", so it has nothing to select in any other kind of evidence. The comment now also says what `entry-id` selects and that it is not an input to `digest`.

**Go changes**:
- Adds `optional=nillable` to `Evidence.Source` which changes this to `*EvidenceMapping` in the generated Go. This change prevents `go-gemara` from creating invalid objects. The current value type is encoded as `"source":{"reference-id":""}` for payload-only evidence, which the new undeclared-source rule rejects.

-->

The `test` commits add fixtures, including negative audit log fixtures for the repeated-in-list, id-reuse and undeclared-source rules, so a regression in the audit log's copies of those rules fails a test.

issue.title: [Feature] Cross-file semantic reference & foreign-key validation (design & placement discussion)
issue.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Currently, Gemara schemas defined in CUE are validated on an isolated, per-document basis (e.g. via `cue vet` or internal test suites). Because each file is evaluated without the context of other documents, cross-artifact foreign-key relationships cannot be statically caught:

1. Dangling Mapping References :- A `MappingDocument` can reference a non-existent control ID in its `source` or `target.entry-id` without failing validation.
2. Undeclared Mapping References :- A document can use a `reference-id` (e.g. in `source-reference` or `evaluations.control`) that is completely absent from its `metadata.mapping-references`.
3. Dangling Policy Mitigations :- A `Policy` can claim to mitigate or accept a `risk-id` that does not exist in the referenced `RiskCatalog`.
4. Dangling Log References :- An `EvaluationLog` or `EnforcementLog` can cite non-existent control or assessment-requirement identifiers.

As Gemara moves toward its 2026 roadmap priority of **Schema Stabilization and Production Tooling**, authors and consumers need a reliable way to ensure referential integrity across multi-file document bundles before publishing or distributing them.

### Describe the solution you'd like

We propose introducing a semantic reference validator that indexes multi-file document bundles and performs two-phase integrity verification :- 

1. Phase 1:- Intra-Document Reference Integrity
   - Verifies that every `reference-id` cited in `#EntryMapping`, `#ArtifactMapping`, `#TypedMapping`, or log evaluations is declared within `metadata.mapping-references`.

2. Phase 2 :- Cross-File Foreign-Key Integrity
   - Indexes all declared entity identifiers across loaded catalogs (Control ids, Assessment Requirement ids, Risk ids, Threat ids, Capability ids, Guideline ids, Vector ids).
   - Resolves target catalogs cited by `reference-id` and verifies that cited `entry-id`s actually exist in the target artifact.
   - Verifies sub-entries (e.g., verifying that assessment-requirement ids exist under the referenced parent control).
   - Intelligently supports inverted mapping relationships (such as `subsumed-by` where targets point back to source catalog entries).

3. Tooling & Ergonomics :-
   - Diagnostic output reporting file paths, document ids, error codes (`undeclared-mapping-reference`, `dangling-entry-reference`) and human-readable context.
   - Flags: `--strict` (treats unresolvable external catalogs as errors) and `--format json` (for machine consumption in CI).

### Describe alternatives you've considered

We would like to open a maintainer and community discussion regarding the architectural placement of this validator :- 

- Alternative 1 :- In `gemara-tools` (`gemaraproj/gemara`)
  - Implement as `gemara-tools validate [paths...]`.
  - Pros :- Directly available in the spec repository to validate test fixtures, regression suites and CI baselines.
  - Cons :- `gemara-tools` is primarily internal spec tooling, not distributed to end users.

- Alternative 2 :- In `grcli` (`gemaraproj/grcli`)
  - Enhance `grcli validate` (which currently wraps `cue vet`) to support multi-file bundle semantic validation.
  - Pros :- User-facing; helps practitioners validate compliance bundles before packing into OCI artifacts and publishing to `grc.store`.
  - Cons :- Requires checking out/installing `grcli` during spec repo CI testing unless decoupled.

- Alternative 3 :- Shared Go Module / Core Package (Recommended)
  - Implement the core indexing and validation engine as an importable Go package (e.g., `github.com/gemaraproj/gemara/pkg/validate` or a shared utility) that both `gemara-tools` (internal) and `grcli` (user-facing) can consume.

### Success Criteria

1. Criterion 1 :- Multi-file document bundles can be scanned and indexed for all declared IDs across core Gemara catalog types.
2. Criterion 2 :- Mappings, policies and evaluation logs referencing non-existent `entry-id`s or undeclared `reference-id`s fail validation with explicit diagnostic messages.
3. Criterion 3 :- Valid document bundles (such as `good-mapping-document.yaml` paired with `good-osps.yml`) validate cleanly with exit code 0.
4. Criterion 4 :- Both human-readable text and machine-readable JSON outputs are supported for CI integration.
5. Criterion 5 :- Consensus reached with maintainers on the placement strategy between `gemara-tools` and `grcli`.

### Additional context

1. Discussed briefly with maintainer @jpower432 in the context of the 2026 Strategic Priorities (Schema Stabilization & Tooling).
2. Another community member may also be exploring related validation ideas; opening this issue to establish a shared design space and collaborate on implementation.
3. A fully functional implementation with 10 comprehensive unit and integration tests has already been built and verified against the existing `test/test-data/` fixtures (PR #550), ready to be adapted wherever the team decides is best.

comment.body:
@nameetsinha7-hue, on jpower432's first question, here's something I tried that might be useful for your answer.

Most cross-document references are structs with a `reference-id`: the mapping types in `mapping_inline.cue`, `#TypedMapping`, and Policy's `CatalogImport` and `GuidanceImport`. So you can walk each artifact definition in the CUE and collect every struct with a `reference-id`, with no hand-kept list. The shape also tells you what to check: an `EntryMapping` names one entry, an `ArtifactMapping` only names the artifact, and a `MultiEntryMapping` lists its entries under `entries[].reference-id`. It also gets the two cases from my #550 comment right without anyone having to know about them: it reports `risks.mitigated[].risk` and `risks.accepted[].risk` as the Policy references, and the control and threat mappings as `MultiEntryMapping`s.

It holds across versions with no code change. The same walk finds 57 paths on v1.1.0, 58 on v1.6.0 and 62 on main (27 of those are the shared `metadata.lexicon` and catalog `extends`/`imports`). The 4 new ones on main are exactly the retention references #513 added.

For "a given schema version", it can load the same module `grcli validate` already uses: `github.com/gemaraproj/gemara@<gemara-version>` from the CUE registry, which every release has published since v1.0.0, or a local checkout with `--spec`. So in this repo's CI, a PR's new reference field would be covered automatically.

Gaps I hit:
- Two lists, EvaluationLog's `assessment-logs` and EnforcementLog's `actions`, don't evaluate on their own because of the conditional rules on them. Walking each conjunct of the list (`Value.Expr()`) fixes that.
- Some references are plain strings with no `reference-id` next to them: a MappingDocument's `mappings[].source` and `targets[].entry-id`, and in Policy, `constraints[].target-id`, `exclusions`, `assessment-plans[].requirement-id` and `retention-obligations[].applies-to`. Those would need a rule, or an attribute like the existing `@gemara(...)` ones.
- I'd use the CUE rather than the generated OpenAPI. `openapi.yaml` is only attached to releases from v1.5.0 on, and the same walk over v1.5.0's finds 12 paths against 58 in the CUE.

On placement, grcli's `internal/refs` already parses `mapping-references`, `lexicon`, and catalog `imports` and `extends` with go-gemara's types, and `grcli unpack --with-references` pulls each grc.store reference at the `version` its mapping reference names. Checking the cited entries could follow from there. One catch: grcli calls the `cue` binary rather than the CUE Go API, so the walk would add that dependency.

The walker is about 60 lines of Go, and I'm happy to paste it if it's useful.

`buildTargetInventoryItem` always wrote the `gemara-resource-id` and `name` props, even when they were empty. OSCAL property values can't be empty (they must match `^\S(.*\S)?$`), so those Assessment Results failed validation. The schema accepts `id: ""` and `name: ""` on a target, so this can come from a YAML log as well as from a log built in Go.

Now each prop is only added when it's set, the same way `buildRelevantEvidence` handles the evidence props. There's a table test for empty, name-only and id-only targets. Without the fix it fails OSCAL validation on the empty props; with it, it passes.

comment.body:
Thanks! Agreed, and it isn't only targets. `#Resource` and `#Actor` both embed `#Entity`, whose `id` and `name` are plain `string`, so an `author` with `id: ""` and `name: ""` passes `cue vet` as well (I checked with `good-capability-catalog.yaml` on main), and most other `id` fields in the schema are plain strings too.

Would you like me to open an issue in gemara for requiring non-empty values on `#Entity`? The pattern OSCAL uses, `^\S(.*\S)?$`, would also rule out leading and trailing spaces. Since it makes validation stricter, it would likely count as a breaking change, so it may want to go in with other schema changes.

issue.title: fix(cue2openapi): project the strict helper rules instead of dropping them
issue.body: ## Description Part of #498. `cue2openapi` strips every CUE `if`, so the rules in the three hidden `_*Strict` helpers never reach `openapi.yaml`. The published schema accepts an assessment that ran without `start`, evidence with neither `payload` nor `source`, and a mapping with no `targets` that isn't `no-match`, all of which CUE rejects. Each of those rules is an `if` that makes one field required. Prep now keeps that kind of `if` when it's inside a helper, and post adds it back as an `anyOf` on `AssessmentLog`, `Evidence` and `Mapping`. As we discussed on #498, the rules belong on those types, so a standalone `AssessmentLog` without `start` is rejected too. A rule that can't be expressed exactly is skipped and reported like the other dropped conditionals. I also added each rule to the `#AssessmentLog` and `#Mapping` doc comments, as `#Evidence` already does, and removed the old comment above `assessment-logs` that was leaking into its description. `bad-evaluation-log-missing-start.yaml` gets the `reference-id` the OpenAPI requires, so it now fails only for `start`. Tested with the new tests in `helperrules_test.go`, `make test`, and `make breaking-check` against v1.6.0. The omitted-conditionals count goes from 23 to 20. Here are the three bad fixtures, and the entry in each that breaks the rule, checked against CUE, the v1.6.0 `openapi.yaml` and this branch: The part I'd most like a second look at is how `prep.go` decides an `if` belongs to a helper (`hiddenHelperName` and `declaresField`). issue.title: Make this repo the canonical source for test fixtures and publish them to grc.store at release
issue.body:
:robot: Drafted with AI assistance.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Test fixtures for Gemara artifacts are scattered across repos. `test/test-data/` in this repo holds about 70 `good-*` and `bad-*` YAML files. They define what the schema accepts and rejects, so they are the source of truth. Downstream repos keep copies, and the copies drift as the schema changes. A fixture added or changed here has no path to the repos that depend on it.

This supersedes gemaraproj/community#14, which proposed a separate centralized testdata repository (`gemara-sample-evidence`) with a sample-data generator. Authoring the fixtures where the schema lives means they change in the same PR as the schema, and the schema's own tests keep them valid.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Author fixtures in this repo only. At release, publish them with `grcli` to grc.store as a bundle that carries the same version as the schema release. Downstream repos fetch the bundle at the schema version they target and stop keeping copies.

The publish step would sit beside the release assets proposed in #500 and use the same downstream dispatch.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

- A separate testdata repository with a generator (gemaraproj/community#14). It adds a second place for fixtures to fall behind the schema.
- Keep copying fixtures by hand. The drift is the problem.
- A git submodule pinned to a tag. It ties consumers to git layout and skips the signing and provenance that grc.store provides.
- A plain tarball release asset. This is the cheapest option, but it has no signed provenance and no registry resolution.

### Success Criteria

- A release publishes a fixture bundle to grc.store at the same version as the schema.
- At least one downstream repo drops its copy and fetches the bundle in CI.
- A fixture added in this repo reaches downstream consumers at the next release with no manual copying.
- A consumer can tell which fixtures should pass and which should fail, and why.

### Additional context

- **Expected failures.** The expected error for each `bad-*` fixture lives in `test/schema_test.go`, not in the YAML. Consumers need that mapping too, so it likely moves into the fixtures or into a manifest in the bundle.
- **Invalid files.** The `bad-*` fixtures fail validation on purpose. It is not confirmed whether `grcli publish` validates before packing. If it does, the bundle needs a way around that, or a separate media type.
- **Versioning.** gemaraproj/community#14 wanted per-version sample data (for example v1.0.0 to v1.3.0). Publishing a bundle at each release gives that, so consumers can pin the version they target.
- **Dropped from community#14.** The community-contributed sample-data generator is out of scope here and can go in a separate proposal.
- **Namespace and credentials.** The Gemara namespace under the OpenSSF org already exists on grc.store. What remains is publishing credentials for this repo's release workflow. Per the `grcli` README, a CI publish authenticates with the workflow's GitHub OIDC token, which takes `permissions: id-token: write` and a one-time trusted-publisher binding for `gemaraproj/gemara` on the hub, with no stored secret.
- **Publish mechanism.** Publishing could run through `grcli` directly or through [gemara-publish-action](https://github.com/gemaraproj/gemara-publish-action) once its redesign (gemaraproj/gemara-publish-action#29) lands. The choice depends on whether the redesigned action can publish a fixture bundle.
- Related: #500, #546, gemaraproj/community#14 (superseded), gemaraproj/community#19 (idiomatic testdata, compatible), gemaraproj/gemara-publish-action#29.

Thanks @nameetsinha7-hue. Yes to asserting exact codes. #550's codes are a better thing to pin than error text, which varies between tools. I'd just keep them with the check that produces them, because the schema check and the reference check can disagree about the same files. Two examples from main:

- `good-evaluation-log-unstarted.yaml` passes `cue vet`, but next to `good-osps.yml`, #550 reports three `dangling-subentry-reference` errors. The log cites `OSPS-AC-01.02` to `.04`, and the catalog only has `.01` under `OSPS-AC-01`. So it's a `good-` file that fails the reference check, and probably a fixture to fix.
- `bad-mapping-document.yaml` fails both, with different messages. `cue vet` gives the `metadata."mapping-references".0.id: incomplete value string` that `schema_test.go` pins (from your #532), and #550 reports `undeclared-mapping-reference` for `SOURCE` and `TARGET`. A single `expected_error` column would have to drop one of them.

So I'd key outcomes by check, with `files` as a list on every row:

```yaml
- files:
    - test/test-data/good-evaluation-log-unstarted.yaml
    - test/test-data/good-osps.yml
  schema:
    valid: true
  references:
    valid: false
    error: dangling-subentry-reference
  reason: the log cites assessment requirements the catalog doesn't declare
```

Keying by check rather than by tool means a row doesn't change if the reference check moves to grcli. It also fits jpower432's same-commit goal: this repo's CI asserts the `schema` outcomes, and grcli checks the `references` outcomes against a release, so a stale expectation fails grcli's tests and never blocks a schema PR. issue.title: feat(cue2openapi): list rules OpenAPI cannot express under x-rules
issue.body:
## Description

Follow-up to #537 for #498.

On #498, @jpower432 suggested an `x-` extension with a short list of rule descriptions for the rules OpenAPI can't express. This adds `x-rules` to each affected schema, next to `x-status`:

    AuditLog:
      x-rules:
        - result ids must be unique, and each result's criteria-reference must name one of the declared criteria

The description is the `//` comment directly above the rule in the CUE, or above the hidden `_unique…` field when the rule is that field's value. The generator already turns doc comments into descriptions elsewhere, so this keeps one source. 18 of the 20 rules had no comment directly above them, so I added one to each, stating what the CUE checks. If a rule the projector drops has no comment, generation now fails and names the file and line, the same way a missing `@gemara(format=...)` does. CONTRIBUTING now says so under "Projection directives".

Each rule goes on the schema of the definition that declares it, so the shared rules sit on `Catalog` and `Metadata` and reach the artifacts that use them through `$ref`.

## Schema Changes

### Schema Changes Made

- [ ] No schema changes
- [x] Audit Log schema (`auditlog.cue`) changes
- [x] Capability Catalog schema (`capabilitycatalog.cue`) changes
- [x] Control Catalog schema (`controlcatalog.cue`) changes
- [x] Enforcement Log schema (`enforcementlog.cue`) changes
- [ ] Evaluation Log schema (`evaluationlog.cue`) changes
- [x] Guidance Catalog schema (`guidancecatalog.cue`) changes
- [x] Mapping Document schema (`mappingdocument.cue`) changes
- [x] Policy Document schema (`policy.cue`) changes
- [x] Principle Catalog schema (`principlecatalog.cue`) changes
- [x] Risk Catalog schema (`riskcatalog.cue`) changes
- [x] Threat Catalog schema (`threatcatalog.cue`) changes
- [x] Vector Catalog schema (`vectorcatalog.cue`) changes
- [x] Other (`collections.cue`, `lexicon.cue`, `metadata.cue`)

### Schema Change Details

Comments only: one `//` line above each rule that had none, plus a blank line `cue fmt` wanted in `metadata.cue`. No fields or types change, so it's backward compatible, and the only generated change is the new `x-rules` lines.

## Testing

- [x] Unit tests added/updated (`rules_test.go`, `prep_test.go`, golden document)
- [x] Manual testing performed (`make test`, `make lintcue`, `make cuefmtcheck`, `make breaking-check` against v1.6.0)

## Related Issues

Closes #498. #537 projected the helper rules OpenAPI can express, and this lists the ones it can't.

## Reviewer Hints

- The EnforcementLog entry reads "when the log's disposition is Clear…". That's what the CUE does today, since `disposition` inside `actions` resolves to the log's field, not the action's (I checked with `cue vet`). I described it as written, and I can open a separate issue if action-level was the intent.
- I left the `@gemara(projectable=false)` notes as they are. They mark a field where the CUE checks more than OpenAPI can, and `x-rules` says what it checks. If you'd rather `x-rules` replace them, I can drop them here or in a follow-up.
- Helper rules from #537 that get skipped as unprojectable still only go to stderr, not `x-rules`. None are skipped today.
- #506, #507 and #539 add rules without a `//` comment, so whichever lands second needs a one-line comment on each. I tested each against this branch; the results and suggested wording are in my comments below.

 ---

## Self-review checklist

- [x] This PR has content that was created with AI assistance.
   - [x]  I have read and followed the [Generative AI Contribution Policy](https://www.linuxfoundation.org/legal/generative-ai).
- [x] I have the experience and knowledge necessary to answer maintainer questions about the content of this PR.

issue.title: Make this repo the canonical source for test fixtures and publish them to grc.store at release
issue.body:
:robot: Drafted with AI assistance.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Test fixtures for Gemara artifacts are scattered across repos. `test/test-data/` in this repo holds about 70 `good-*` and `bad-*` YAML files. They define what the schema accepts and rejects, so they are the source of truth. Downstream repos keep copies, and the copies drift as the schema changes. A fixture added or changed here has no path to the repos that depend on it.

This supersedes gemaraproj/community#14, which proposed a separate centralized testdata repository (`gemara-sample-evidence`) with a sample-data generator. Authoring the fixtures where the schema lives means they change in the same PR as the schema, and the schema's own tests keep them valid.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Author fixtures in this repo only. At release, publish them with `grcli` to grc.store as a bundle that carries the same version as the schema release. Downstream repos fetch the bundle at the schema version they target and stop keeping copies.

The publish step would sit beside the release assets proposed in #500 and use the same downstream dispatch.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

- A separate testdata repository with a generator (gemaraproj/community#14). It adds a second place for fixtures to fall behind the schema.
- Keep copying fixtures by hand. The drift is the problem.
- A git submodule pinned to a tag. It ties consumers to git layout and skips the signing and provenance that grc.store provides.
- A plain tarball release asset. This is the cheapest option, but it has no signed provenance and no registry resolution.

### Success Criteria

- A release publishes a fixture bundle to grc.store at the same version as the schema.
- At least one downstream repo drops its copy and fetches the bundle in CI.
- A fixture added in this repo reaches downstream consumers at the next release with no manual copying.
- A consumer can tell which fixtures should pass and which should fail, and why.

### Additional context

- **Expected failures.** The expected error for each `bad-*` fixture lives in `test/schema_test.go`, not in the YAML. Consumers need that mapping too, so it likely moves into the fixtures or into a manifest in the bundle.
- **Invalid files.** The `bad-*` fixtures fail validation on purpose. It is not confirmed whether `grcli publish` validates before packing. If it does, the bundle needs a way around that, or a separate media type.
- **Versioning.** gemaraproj/community#14 wanted per-version sample data (for example v1.0.0 to v1.3.0). Publishing a bundle at each release gives that, so consumers can pin the version they target.
- **Dropped from community#14.** The community-contributed sample-data generator is out of scope here and can go in a separate proposal.
- **Namespace and credentials.** The Gemara namespace under the OpenSSF org already exists on grc.store. What remains is publishing credentials for this repo's release workflow. Per the `grcli` README, a CI publish authenticates with the workflow's GitHub OIDC token, which takes `permissions: id-token: write` and a one-time trusted-publisher binding for `gemaraproj/gemara` on the hub, with no stored secret.
- **Publish mechanism.** Publishing could run through `grcli` directly or through [gemara-publish-action](https://github.com/gemaraproj/gemara-publish-action) once its redesign (gemaraproj/gemara-publish-action#29) lands. The choice depends on whether the redesigned action can publish a fixture bundle.
- Related: #500, #546, gemaraproj/community#14 (superseded), gemaraproj/community#19 (idiomatic testdata, compatible), gemaraproj/gemara-publish-action#29.

I tried a `--dry-run` publish of `bad-no-groups.yaml` and got a bundle back with no complaint, so the `bad-*` files should be fine on the client side. issue.title: Stop ObjectStorage journal failures from failing durable tasks
issue.body:
On Airflow before 3.3, durable agent tasks keep their journal in a JSON file through ObjectStorage. When that storage failed, or the file was damaged, the journal could fail a task whose work had already succeeded, or quietly throw away the previous attempt's steps. This makes that backend behave like the task state store one already does: storage problems are logged and skipped, and they never fail the task.

**What was wrong**

`DurableStorageProtocol` says a backend may skip a write it can't make without failing the step, and `TaskStateStoreDurableStorage` (Airflow >= 3.3) already does. `DurableStorage` didn't: an error from `_write` went straight out of `save_step`. Most saves happen after the work they record, so a failed write could:

- fail a task whose work had already succeeded, when the journal lists more than one agent run, because `DurableJournal.cleanup` rewrites the run list through `save_step`
- raise a storage error in place of the agent's own error, because `DurableRun.fail` saves the run meta before re-raising
- fail a tool step after the tool's side effect had already run

Reads had problems too. A read that failed with an `OSError` was treated as an empty journal without a warning, so the next save overwrote the previous attempt's steps. A file holding JSON that isn't an object failed the task with an `AttributeError` on the first lookup.

**What changes**

- A failed write is skipped with a warning and `save_step` returns `False`, so a retry runs that step again. In memory the key keeps its previous value, so a later save doesn't write the skipped entry either.
- If the journal file can't be read, for a reason other than being missing or invalid, it's left in place for the next attempt. This attempt runs live without recording, and `delete_steps` leaves the file alone.
- A file that isn't a valid journal is logged and replaced: one cut off mid-write, JSON that isn't an object, or bytes that aren't UTF-8 text. The last case is the second commit. Without it, such a file counted as unreadable, so that task instance would never journal again.

The durable execution docs now describe this for the ObjectStorage backend too.

**Testing**

On Linux (WSL, Ubuntu 24.04) the durable tests give 302 passed and 3 skipped, because the optional `agents` and `strands` packages aren't installed. There's also 1 error, in `TestSummary.test_summary_names_the_tools_a_retry_runs_again`. That test runs on the in-memory test storage and doesn't touch this code; the error is a local fixture import (`cap_structlog` needs `airflow_shared`, which isn't installed in a plain uv env).

I wrote the non-UTF-8 case test-first: it failed before the fix and passes after. While developing the first commit, each new guard in `storage.py` was removed one at a time, and a test failed every time. The prek pre-commit hooks pass.

<details>
<summary>Test runs (WSL, Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.12.16)</summary>

New case before the fix (`f8165fb566` with only the test change applied):

```
$ uv run --project providers/common/ai pytest providers/common/ai/tests/unit/common/ai/durable/test_storage.py -k corrupt -v
...test_a_corrupt_journal_is_reported_and_started_over[cut off mid-write] PASSED
...test_a_corrupt_journal_is_reported_and_started_over[not a JSON object] PASSED
...test_a_corrupt_journal_is_reported_and_started_over[not UTF-8 text] FAILED
E   AssertionError: assert False
E    +  where False = save_step('k', {...})
1 failed, 2 passed, 20 deselected
```

After the fix:

```
...test_a_corrupt_journal_is_reported_and_started_over[not UTF-8 text] PASSED
3 passed, 20 deselected
```

Full durable suite:

```
$ uv run --project providers/common/ai pytest providers/common/ai/tests/unit/common/ai/durable -q
302 passed, 3 skipped, 1 warning, 1 error
ERROR ...test_journal.py::TestSummary::test_summary_names_the_tools_a_retry_runs_again - ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'airflow_shared'
```

</details>

issue.body: Converting an EvaluationLog to OSCAL Assessment Results produces invalid OSCAL whenever a result isn't Passed or Failed. The converter copies the Gemara result straight into `finding.target.status.reason`, but OSCAL expects a token there, so "Not Run", "Needs Review" and "Not Applicable" fail validation because of the spaces. You can see it with the `pvtr-baseline-scan.yaml` fixture from the gemara repo: 23 errors for "Not Run" and 4 for "Needs Review". It slipped through because the CI export only uses a log with Passed and Failed results, and the AR tests only checked that the JSON round-trips (the gap jmeridth mentioned in #133). What I changed: - Results other than Passed and Failed now map to `not-run`, `needs-review`, `not-applicable` and `unknown`. A value outside the Result enum can't come from a valid EvaluationLog, so it maps to `invalid`. The state stays the same. I left the enums alone, since ADR 0013 keeps Title Case for the people writing Gemara. - The AR tests now validate against the OSCAL schema (the helper is renamed to `assertValidOSCAL`), and the mapping table also covers Not Run and an unrecognized value. - `makeEvaluationLog` in `sarif_test.go` now sets a Target. Without one, the inventory item ends up with empty props, which fail once the schema check runs. SARIF doesn't use it. **Behaviour change:** anyone reading `status.reason` will see new values. `Unknown` is now `unknown`, and Not Run, Needs Review and Not Applicable (which never validated before) are now `not-run`, `needs-review` and `not-applicable`. Anything matching the old strings needs updating. To try it, with gemara checked out next to go-gemara: ``` go install github.com/defenseunicorns/go-oscal@v0.7.1 go run ./cmd/oscalexport evaluation ../gemara/test/test-data/pvtr-baseline-scan.yaml --output /tmp/ar.json go-oscal validate -f /tmp/ar.json ``` On main it fails on `status/reason`; on this branch it validates: Related to #29

comment.body: Thanks @jpower432! I'll take the `buildTargetInventoryItem` guard as a follow-up so the `Target` workaround in `makeEvaluationLog` can go.

issue.title: Preserve CUE-only semantic constraints in generated OpenAPI
issue.body:
### Version of Gemara

`main` at `24e52e9`

### Describe the bug

The generated OpenAPI projection drops constraints represented through hidden strict definitions. `#_AssessmentLogStrict` makes `start` required when an assessment actually executed, but the generator resolves the reference to base `#AssessmentLog` and loses the conditional requirement. A consumer using `openapi.yaml` can accept a document that the authoritative CUE schema rejects.

The same projection pattern applies to `#_EvidenceStrict`, so the payload-or-source constraint fixed in #475 is not expressed in OpenAPI.

### To Reproduce

1. Inspect `evaluationlog.cue:34-42` and `evaluationlog.cue:72-74`.
2. Generate `openapi.yaml` with `gemara cue2openapi`.
3. Validate through the generated `AssessmentLog` schema an executed assessment without `start`, or evidence with neither `payload` nor `source`.
4. Compare with CUE validation, which rejects those documents.

### Expected behavior

The projection must not silently omit constraints OpenAPI can represent. Constraints that OpenAPI cannot represent must be surfaced as explicit documentation or extension metadata, with generated-schema tests covering both strict variants.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Additional context

Breakdown item 7 from [#488](https://github.com/gemaraproj/gemara/issues/488#issuecomment-5672005832). This is separate from field and regex projection defects in #468, #473, and #474. Relevant generator behavior: `cmd/internal/cmd/converter.go:43-48`.

comment.body:
Hi @jpower432, I'd like to pick this up in small pieces, starting with the three hidden helpers: `#_AssessmentLogStrict`, `#_EvidenceStrict` and `#_MappingStrict`.

Each of their rules is an `if` whose body only makes one field required, so prep can recognise it instead of dropping it, and post can add it back as an `anyOf` next to every reference to the helper, before the collapse. Anything it can't project exactly (another shape, a defaulted or optional field and so on) is left out and reported, the same as today.

I have it working locally. The omitted count goes from 23 to 20, and the bad fixtures for these three rules, which the v1.6.0 `openapi.yaml` accepts, are rejected by the generated one:

```
document                                 CUE       v1.6.0 openapi.yaml   generated
bad-evaluation-log-missing-start.yaml    rejected  accepted              rejected
bad-audit-log-evidence-neither.yaml      rejected  accepted              rejected
bad-mapping-no-target.yaml               rejected  accepted              rejected
```

The first fixture has `requirement.reference-id` added; without it the file already fails on the reference-id gap, so it can't show the start rule. It also applies cleanly on top of #507.

Two questions before I open a PR:

1. The rules go where the helper is used, not on `AssessmentLog`, `Evidence` or `Mapping`, since the base definitions don't have them in CUE either. So a standalone `AssessmentLog` without `start` still validates, which is what step 3 in the issue does. Is that what you'd want, or should the base schemas carry them too?
2. For the rules OpenAPI can't express (mostly unique ids and cross-references), would you rather have an `x-` extension listing them on the schema, or keep the `projectable=false` caveat?

issue.title: Add QdrantSearchOperator for vector similarity search
issue.body:
Replaces #69673, which was closed under the open-PR limit and can't be reopened from my side. Same commits, rebased onto main with no conflicts.

The Qdrant provider can write vectors with `QdrantIngestOperator` but has no operator to read them back, so a similarity search from a Dag means calling `hook.conn.query_points` directly and converting the returned `ScoredPoint` objects to dicts by hand before they can go to XCom.

issue.title: Fingerprint durable agent steps that hold sets or values that are not JSON
issue.body:
Durable execution checks each recorded step against a fingerprint of the request before it replays it. On main that fingerprint is `json.dumps` of the raw tool arguments and settings, plus pydantic's JSON dump of the message history and request parameters, which leaves two gaps:

- **A value that isn't plain JSON fingerprints as `None`.** A `datetime` or `Decimal` tool argument, a dataclass in `tool_choice`, bytes or a non-string dict key all fail `json.dumps`, so those steps replay without verification.
- **Sets hash in hash-seed order.** Every task attempt is a new process, so a fingerprint that covers a `set[str]` changes between attempts. `ModelRequestParameters.revealed_tool_names` is one whenever tool search is used, so the run diverges at that step on retry and everything after it runs again.

This PR fingerprints tool arguments and settings from pydantic's rendering (`to_jsonable_python`), and orders the members of a set by their JSON encoding wherever one appears. Plain JSON arguments and settings, and a message history without sets, hash exactly as on main.

### Design rationale

- **Sets are found, not guessed.** The JSON rendering is paired with pydantic's python-mode dump of the same payload, which keeps sets as sets. A list is sorted only where it holds exactly the members of the set at that place, so a list a serializer produced keeps its order.
- **What can't be told apart is refused rather than hashed:** dict keys that collide once rendered (`1` and `"1"`, `b"a"` and `"a"` inside a model), anything that renders through an iterator, and a set of strings that a JSON-only serializer renamed or reshaped.
- **Tool arguments are rendered from copies**, so a computed field, cached property or serializer can't change what the tool receives, and a lazily validated `Iterable` argument is never read before the tool runs.
- **When the python-mode dump itself fails**, as it does for a set of models or (from pydantic 2.13) a dict keyed by one, the history falls back to main's digest.
- **Failures degrade, never raise.** A request that can't be fingerprinted gets `None`, and the warning names the step and the cause (`step=`, `error=`, `error_type=`).

### Now on top of AirflowDurability

#74385 replaced `CachingModel` and `CachingToolset` with a journal while this PR was in review. This PR originally changed those wrappers so that a step without a fingerprint was never replayed. The journal already handles that case its own way: such a step replays only when its name matches and the step before it replayed, so it is never matched against a different conversation. That guard is dropped, and the fingerprint changes now feed the journal. `durable_execution.rst` describes what can and can't be fingerprinted in terms of the journal.

issue.body:
## Summary

- remove Hermes dotenv-owned variables from environments inherited by Desktop-spawned profile backends
- include root and named-profile `.env` and `.op.env` secret scopes
- apply isolation to primary, sticky-profile, and pooled-profile backend launches
- preserve unrelated OS/runtime variables and Windows environment-key casing

## Root Cause

Hermes Desktop spread its full `process.env` into every backend child. When the Desktop process contained credentials loaded for another profile, those credentials remained present before the selected profile scope was applied.

Platform adapters and external secret sources could then use inherited credentials, causing multiple profiles to connect with the same identity or expose another profile's secret scope.

## Fix

The Desktop backend environment resolver now collects variable names declared by root and named-profile `.env` and `.op.env` files, then removes those variables from the inherited parent environment before starting a profile backend.

`buildPoolBackendSpawnEnv()` and `buildPrimaryBackendSpawnEnv()` are used by `spawnPoolBackend()` and `startHermes()`, respectively. The selected profile's existing dotenv loader then reloads only its own secret scope.

Secret values are never logged or included in diagnostics.

## Tests

- added filesystem-backed root/profile `.env` and `.op.env` isolation coverage
- added behavior-level assertions for pooled and primary backend spawn environments
- added Windows case-insensitive environment-key coverage
- verified unrelated environment variables remain available
- focused Electron tests: **13/13 passed**
- Electron TypeScript check: **passed**
- ESLint on touched files: **passed**
- Electron main-process production bundle: **passed**
- branch rebased onto current `main`

Fixes #68367

issue.title: [ATen] Add reduction tag to missing base reduction ops (re-land of #188902)

labels.name: repo-83a6ea0f
labels.description: This issue has been looked at a team member, and triaged and prioritized into an appropriate module

issue.body:
Re-land of #188902 with the fix for the MPS `mode` OpInfo interaction that caused the original PR to be auto-reverted.

### What was reverted

#188902 added the `reduction` tag to 14 `native_functions.yaml` entries. That caused `test/test_ops.py::test_reduction_ops_reduce` to be generated for the `mode` op for the first time. The new test `test_reduction_ops_reduce_mode_mps` failed with `Unexpected success` on trunk, triggering the auto-revert.

### Root cause

1. `test_reduction_ops_reduce` is parametrized over ops with `torch.Tag.reduction`
2. Before #188902, `mode` had no tag, so the test was never generated for it
3. After the tag was added, `test_reduction_ops_reduce_mode_mps` is created
4. `mode`'s OpInfo carries a blanket `TestCommon` `expectedFailure` on MPS, because `aten::mode` dispatches to `CPU, CUDA, XPU` only
5. The test's per-sample loop does `if "dim" not in sample.kwargs: continue`, and `sample_inputs_mode` passed `dim` **positionally** — so every sample was skipped and `aten::mode` was never invoked
6. Trivial pass + `expectedFailure` = `Unexpected success` = red trunk

Nothing was wrong with the tag additions themselves. The failure came entirely from the interaction between the `mode` OpInfo's blanket decorator and the newly-generated test.

### Fix

`sample_inputs_mode` now passes `dim` and `keepdim` as **kwargs** instead of positionally. No new decorators are added and no existing ones are touched.

With this change `test_reduction_ops_reduce` actually invokes `aten::mode`:

- On CPU/CUDA/XPU, `torch.mode(x, dim=k)` returns a `(values, indices)` namedtuple. The test's `isinstance(result, torch.Tensor)` guard skips the numel assertion for those samples, as intended.
- On MPS, `aten::mode` raises `NotImplementedError`, which the existing blanket `expectedFailure` catches as an expected failure.
- If MPS support is added later, that xfail will fire `Unexpected success` and prompt its removal — preserving the maintenance signal @Skylion007 asked for, rather than silencing it with a skip.

Fixing this at the sample-inputs level addresses the cause rather than suppressing the symptom.

### Newly tagged ops

- `nanmean`, `nanmean.out` (mirrors `mean.*`)
- `median`, `median.dim`, `median.dim_values`
- `nanmedian`, `nanmedian.dim`, `nanmedian.dim_values` (mirror `min.dim` / `max.dim`)
- `mode`, `mode.values` (dim-reduced like `min.dim`)
- `trace` (sum over diagonal -> scalar)
- `dist` (`norm(a - b)` -> scalar)
- `special_logsumexp`, `special_logsumexp.out` (mirrors `logsumexp.*`)

### Audit of the other tagged ops

Confirmed none share the MPS blanket-xfail interaction that `mode` had:

| Op | OpInfo state on MPS |
| --- | --- |
| `nanmean` | No blanket xfail |
| `median` | `dtypesIfMPS` set -> supported |
| `nanmedian` | `dtypesIfMPS` set -> supported |
| `trace` | `dtypesIfMPS` set -> supported |
| `dist` | No blanket xfail |
| `special_logsumexp` (via `logsumexp`) | No blanket xfail |

### Diff summary

- `aten/src/ATen/native/native_functions.yaml`: +14 (unchanged from #188902)
- `torch/testing/_internal/common_methods_invocations.py`: +16 / -12 (`sample_inputs_mode`)

Total: 2 files, +30 / -12.

### Context

Follow-up to #129020, per @eellison's invitation on #169944 ("if there are any missing ops, please submit a pr to add them").

cc @eellison @drisspg

One thing I noticed with the per-call client and `auth_type="workload_identity"`: the SDK keeps the exchanged token on the client's `WorkloadIdentityAuth`, so a new client per call also means a new token exchange per call.
